definition: Following a target object across video frames, maintaining its identity through occlusion and appearance change.
details: Following a target object across video frames, maintaining its identity through occlusion and appearance change.

explainer.lead: Visual tracking follows a target object across video frames, maintaining its identity through occlusion and appearance change. It lets a system keep track of what it is watching over time.

tiers.eli5: Like keeping your eye on a friend in a crowd as people walk in front of them and the light changes.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers initialise a tracker on a target and update it frame by frame; a common pitfall is losing the target during long occlusions or when its appearance changes sharply.
tiers.paperLevel: Following a target object across video frames while maintaining its identity through occlusion and appearance change; robustness is limited by occlusions and appearance shifts.

explainer.example: A tracker follows a car through a tunnel, reacquiring it when it emerges from the dark.
